nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 2$, let $d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \ge 0\}$. If there are a real number $\delta > 0$ and an integer $N \ge 1$ such that $d_{n+1} \ge \left(2 + \frac{1}{r-1} + \delta\right) d_n$ for every $n \ge N - 1$, then $D$ is not $r$-accessible.
nodes.title: Growth bound for the degree of accessibility

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$ and $r$ be natural numbers and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. If $A$ is $rd$-accessible, then the set $\{a \in A : d \mid a\}$ of members of $A$ divisible by $d$ is $r$-accessible.
nodes.title: Multiples of $d$ in an accessible set

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$ and $r$ be natural numbers and let $A$ be a set of natural numbers. If $A$ is $rd$-accessible, then the set $\{n \ge 1 : nd \in A\}$, that is, the positive integers of the form $a/d$ with $a \in A$, is $r$-accessible.
nodes.title: Integral quotients of an accessible set

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 2$ and $c$ be natural numbers, let $D$ be a set of positive integers, and write $D + c = \{d + c : d \in D\}$. Suppose that for every coloring of $D$ with $r - 1$ colors and every $k \ge 1$ there are $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1} \in D$, all of the same color, that form a $(D + c)$-diffsequence, that is, $x_{i+1} - x_i \in D + c$ for every $i < k - 1$. Then $D + c$ is $r$-accessible.
nodes.title: A coloring criterion for accessibility of a shifted set

nodes.summary: Let $D$, $D_1$ and $D_2$ be sets of natural numbers with $D = D_1 \cup D_2$. If $D$ is accessible, then $D_1$ is accessible or $D_2$ is accessible.
nodes.title: One part of an accessible union is accessible

nodes.summary: Let $r \ge 1$, let $d_0 < d_1 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \ge 0\}$. Suppose there are real numbers $\alpha$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $n$ the fractional part of $\alpha d_n$ lies in the closed interval $[\varepsilon, (r-1)/r]$. Then there is a coloring of the positive integers with $r$ colors that has no monochromatic…
nodes.title: Colorings avoiding long diffsequences under fractional-part bounds

nodes.summary: The set of prime numbers is $2$-accessible: for every colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ of the natural numbers with two colours and every length $k \ne 1$ there is a sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers, all of the same colour, such that each difference $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is a prime number.
nodes.title: The primes are 2-accessible

nodes.summary: The statement that the set of prime numbers is $2$-accessible: for every colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, 1\}$ of the natural numbers with two colours and every length $k \ne 1$ there is a sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers, all of the same colour, such that each difference $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is a prime number. Open Problem Garden question OPG-1797 asks whether this holds.
nodes.title: 2-accessibility of the primes

nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ denote the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. The even Fibonacci set $\{F_{3n+3} : n \ge 0\} = \{2, 8, 34, \dots\}$ is not $2$-accessible.
nodes.title: The even Fibonacci set is not 2-accessible

nodes.summary: The even Fibonacci set $\{2, 8, 34, \dots\}$ is $1$-accessible, and it is not $r$-accessible for any natural number $r \ge 2$.
nodes.title: The even Fibonacci numbers have degree of accessibility $1$

nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ denote the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. The even Fibonacci set is $\{F_{3n+3} : n \ge 0\}$; its first terms are $2, 8, 34, \dots$.
nodes.title: Even Fibonacci set

nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ denote the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$, and let $E = \{F_{3n+3} : n \ge 0\} = \{2, 8, 34, \dots\}$ be the even Fibonacci set. There is a coloring of the positive integers with $2$ colors under which no four positive integers $x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3$ of the same color satisfy $x_{i+1} - x_i \in E$ for $i = 0, 1, 2$.
nodes.title: A 2-coloring with no monochromatic 4-term even-Fibonacci diffsequence

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ be the $n$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$, and let $\varphi = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ be the golden ratio. For every natural number $n \ge 2$,
nodes.title: Fibonacci numbers divided by the golden ratio

nodes.summary: There is a coloring of the positive integers with two colors that admits no monochromatic $5$-term arithmetic progression with gap in the positive Fibonacci set $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots\}$, that is, no positive integers $x_0, \dots, x_4$ of one color with $x_i = a + i d$ for all $i < 5$, for a positive integer $a$ and a positive Fibonacci number $d$. Moreover, the positive Fibonacci set is $1$-large, and it is not…
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions with Fibonacci gaps are not $2$-regular

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. The positive Fibonacci set $\{F_n : n \ge 2\} = \{1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots\}$ is not $2$-large.
nodes.title: The positive Fibonacci set is not 2-large

nodes.title: The morphism $\nu$

nodes.summary: The positive Fibonacci set $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots\}$ is not $r$-accessible for any natural number $r \ge 4$. Moreover, some coloring of the positive integers with four colors admits no monochromatic $4$-term diffsequence with differences in the positive Fibonacci set: there are no positive integers $x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3$ of one color such that $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is a positive Fibonacci number for $i = 0, 1, 2$.
nodes.title: The Fibonacci numbers have degree of accessibility at most $3$

nodes.summary: There is a coloring of the positive integers with two colors such that no 6-term arithmetic progression $a, a + d, \dots, a + 5d$ of positive integers whose gap $d$ is a positive Fibonacci number is monochromatic.
nodes.title: A 2-coloring with no monochromatic 6-term progression with positive Fibonacci gap

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all lacunary sets $D_1, \dots, D_n$, the union $D_1 \cup \dots \cup D_n$ is not 2-large.
nodes.title: Finite unions of lacunary sets are not 2-large

nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ be the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. The number $4$ belongs to the set $G = \{F_{3n}/2 : n \ge 1\} = \{1, 4, 17, 72, \dots\}$ of halves of the positive even Fibonacci numbers; indeed $4 = F_6/2$.
nodes.title: $4$ is half of an even Fibonacci number

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ be the $n$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$, let $\varphi = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ be the golden ratio, so that $2\varphi - 1 = \sqrt{5}$, and write $\{y\} = y - \lfloor y \rfloor$ for the fractional part. Let $n \ge 13$ be a natural number and $\varepsilon \in \{-4, 0, 4\}$, let $c_{n,\varepsilon}$ be Wesley's constant, which depends on $n \bmod 4$ and $\varepsilon$, and put…
nodes.title: Fractional parts of shifted Fibonacci numbers divided by $\sqrt{5}$

nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ be the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$, let $\varphi = (1 + \sqrt{5})/2$ be the golden ratio, and write $\{y\} = y - \lfloor y \rfloor$ for the fractional part. Let $i \ge 1$ be a natural number, put $g_i = F_{3i}/2$ (an integer, since $F_{3i}$ is even), and let $x_1, x_2, m_1, m_2$ be integers. Then: (i) if $g_i$ is even, $2(x_2 - x_1) = g_i$, $x_1 = \lfloor m_1\varphi \rfloor$ and…
nodes.title: Differences of fractional parts of multiples of the golden ratio

For a homeomorphism $T$ and an integer $a$, write $T^{-a}(U)$ for the preimage of $U$ under the $a$-th power of $T$. Then the following three conditions are equivalent: (a) for every coloring of $\mathbb{Z}$ with $r$…
nodes.title: Furstenberg–Weiss correspondence for translation-invariant families

nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ be the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. The set of halves of the positive even Fibonacci numbers is $G = \{F_{3n}/2 : n \ge 1\} = \{1, 4, 17, 72, \dots\}$; its elements are written $g_n = F_{3n}/2$ for $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Halves of even Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is accessible if and only if it is $r$-accessible for every natural number $r \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Accessibility means $r$-accessibility for every $r \ge 1$

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is accessible if it is $r$-accessible for every natural number $r \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Accessible sets

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is chromatically intersective if and only if every element of $D$ is positive and, for every natural number $r \ge 1$ and every coloring of the positive integers with $r$ colors, there are positive integers $a$ and $b$ of the same color whose difference $a - b$, computed in the integers, lies in $D$.
nodes.title: Characterization of chromatically intersective sets

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is chromatically intersective if every element of $D$ is positive and, for every natural number $r \ge 1$ and every coloring of the positive integers with $r$ colors, there are positive integers $a$ and $b$ of the same color whose difference $a - b$, computed in the integers, lies in $D$.
nodes.title: Chromatically intersective sets

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of natural numbers, $k$ a natural number and $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ positive integers. Then $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ is a $k$-term arithmetic progression with gap in $D$ if and only if there are a positive integer $a$ and an element $d \in D$ such that $x_i = a + i d$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: Characterization of arithmetic progressions with gap in $D$

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of natural numbers and $k$ a natural number. A sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of positive integers is a $k$-term arithmetic progression with gap in $D$ if there are a positive integer $a$ and an element $d \in D$ such that $x_i = a + i d$ for every $i < k$.
nodes.title: Arithmetic progressions with gap in $D$

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of natural numbers and $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ integers. Then $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ is a $D$-diffsequence if and only if for every $i$ with $i + 1 < k$ there is $d \in D$ such that $x_{i+1} - x_i = d$.
nodes.title: Characterization of $D$-diffsequences

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of natural numbers and $k$ a natural number. A finite sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of integers is a $D$-diffsequence when for every $i$ with $i + 1 < k$ there is $d \in D$ with $x_{i+1} - x_i = d$.
nodes.title: $D$-diffsequences

nodes.summary: A sequence $(m_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers is lacunary if and only if $m_n > 0$ for every $n$ and there is a real number $q > 1$ such that $m_{n+1} \ge q \, m_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Characterization of lacunary sequences

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is lacunary if and only if there is a lacunary sequence $(m_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers with $D = \{m_n : n \ge 0\}$.
nodes.title: Characterization of lacunary sets

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is lacunary when $D = \{m_n : n \ge 0\}$ for some lacunary sequence $(m_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers.
nodes.title: Lacunary set

nodes.summary: A sequence $(m_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers is lacunary when $m_n > 0$ for every $n$ and there is a real number $\lambda > 1$ such that $m_{n+1} \ge \lambda m_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Lacunary sequence

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is large if and only if it is $r$-large for every natural number $r \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Characterization of large sets

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is large when it is $r$-large for every natural number $r \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Large set

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ be a natural number and $D$ a set of natural numbers. Then $D$ is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence if and only if every element of $D$ is positive and, for every compact metric space $X$, every minimal homeomorphism $T \colon X \to X$ and every nonempty open set $U \subseteq X$, there is $d \in D$ such that $\bigcap_{j=0}^{\ell} T^{-jd}(U)$ is nonempty, where $T^{-jd}(U)$ is the preimage of $U$…
nodes.title: Characterization of $\ell$-topological recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $\ell$ be a natural number. A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence when every element of $D$ is positive and, for every compact metric space $X$, every minimal homeomorphism $T \colon X \to X$ and every nonempty open set $U \subseteq X$, there is $d \in D$ such that $\bigcap_{j=0}^{\ell} T^{-jd}(U)$ is nonempty, where $T^{-jd}(U)$ is the preimage of $U$ under the $jd$-th iterate…
nodes.title: Sets of $\ell$-topological recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and $T \colon X \to X$ a homeomorphism. Then $T$ is minimal if and only if there is no closed set $K \subseteq X$ with $K \ne \emptyset$, $K \ne X$ and $T(K) = K$.
nodes.title: Characterization of minimal systems

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and $T$ a homeomorphism of $X$. The system $(X, T)$ is minimal when there is no closed set $K \subseteq X$ that is nonempty, different from $X$ and invariant, meaning $T(K) = K$.
nodes.title: Minimal system

nodes.summary: Given a colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, r - 1\}$ of the natural numbers with $r$ colours, a finite sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers is monochromatic when all its terms have the same colour: $c(x_i) = c(x_j)$ for all $i, j < k$.
nodes.title: Monochromatic finite sequences

nodes.summary: Let $r$ and $k$ be natural numbers and let $c$ color the positive integers with the colors $0, 1, \dots, r - 1$. A sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of positive integers is monochromatic for $c$ when $c(x_i) = c(x_j)$ for all $i, j < k$.
nodes.title: Monochromatic sequences of positive integers

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of multiple topological recurrence if and only if $D$ is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for every natural number $\ell \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Characterization of multiple topological recurrence

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of multiple topological recurrence when it is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for every natural number $\ell \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Sets of multiple topological recurrence

nodes.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is $r$-accessible when for every colouring $c : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, r - 1\}$ with $r$ colours and every length $k \ne 1$ there is a sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers that is monochromatic for $c$ and is an $S$-diffsequence: for each $i$ with $i + 1 < k$ there is $d \in S$ with $x_{i+1} = x_i + d$.
nodes.title: $r$-accessible sets of natural numbers

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number and $D$ a set of natural numbers. nodes.title: Characterization of $r$-accessible sets

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. A set $D$ of natural numbers is $r$-accessible when every element of $D$ is positive, $r \ge 1$, and for every coloring $c$ of the positive integers with the colors $0, 1, \dots, r - 1$ and every natural number $k \ge 1$ there are positive integers $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ that are monochromatic for $c$ and form a $D$-diffsequence: $x_{i+1} - x_i \in D$, the difference taken in the…
nodes.title: $r$-accessibility for colorings of the positive integers

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number and $D$ a set of natural numbers. Then $D$ is $r$-large if and only if every element of $D$ is positive, $r \ge 1$, and for every coloring $c$ of the positive integers with the colors $0, 1, \dots, r - 1$ and every natural number $k \ge 1$ there are positive integers $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ that are monochromatic for $c$ and form a $D$-AP: there are a positive integer $a$ and some…
nodes.title: Characterization of $r$-large sets

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. A set $D$ of natural numbers is $r$-large when every element of $D$ is positive, $r \ge 1$, and for every coloring $c$ of the positive integers with the colors $0, 1, \dots, r - 1$ and every natural number $k \ge 1$ there are positive integers $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ that are monochromatic for $c$ and form a $D$-AP: there are a positive integer $a$ and some $d \in D$ with $x_i = a + i d$…
nodes.title: $r$-large sets

nodes.summary: For a set $S$ of natural numbers, a finite sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of natural numbers is an $S$-diffsequence when each term is the previous one plus an element of $S$: for every $i$ with $i + 1 < k$ there is $d \in S$ with $x_{i+1} = x_i + d$.
nodes.title: Finite $S$-diffsequences

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of topological recurrence if and only if it is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for $\ell = 1$.
nodes.title: Topological recurrence is $1$-topological recurrence

nodes.summary: A set $D$ of natural numbers is a set of topological recurrence when it is a set of $\ell$-topological recurrence for $\ell = 1$.
nodes.title: Sets of topological recurrence

nodes.summary: For a homeomorphism $T$ of a topological space $X$, an integer $s$ and a subset $U \subseteq X$, the iterated preimage $T^{-s} U$ is the preimage $(T^s)^{-1}(U)$ of $U$ under the $s$-th power $T^s$ of $T$ in the group of homeomorphisms of $X$.
nodes.title: Iterated preimage as a preimage under a power

nodes.summary: For a homeomorphism $T$ of a topological space $X$, an integer $s$ and a subset $U \subseteq X$, the iterated preimage $T^{-s} U$ is defined as the preimage $(T^s)^{-1}(U)$ of $U$ under the $s$-th power $T^s$ of $T$ in the group of homeomorphisms of $X$.
nodes.title: Iterated preimage

nodes.summary: Let $\ell \ge 1$ and let $S_0, \dots, S_{\ell-1} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be lacunary sets with union $S = \bigcup_i S_i$. Then there are real numbers $\alpha$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the infimum over $s \in S$ of the distance $|\alpha s - \operatorname{round}(\alpha s)|$ from $\alpha s$ to its nearest integer $\operatorname{round}(\alpha s)$ equals $\varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Dilates of a finite union of lacunary sets stay away from the integers

nodes.summary: If $D_1, D_2 \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and their union $D = D_1 \cup D_2$ is large, then $D_1$ is large or $D_2$ is large.
nodes.title: Largeness is partition regular

nodes.summary: Let $L = \{2, 1, 3, 4, 7, \dots\}$ be the set of Lucas numbers $L_0 = 2$, $L_1 = 1$, $L_{n+2} = L_{n+1} + L_n$. There is a coloring of the positive integers with the colors $0, 1, 2, 3$ for which no sequence $x_0, x_1, x_2$ of positive integers is both monochromatic and an $L$-diffsequence; and $L$ is not $r$-accessible for any $r \ge 4$.
nodes.title: The Lucas numbers are not $4$-accessible

nodes.summary: Write $F_m$ for the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. A natural number $d$ belongs to the even Fibonacci set if and only if $d = F_{3n+3}$ for some natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Membership in the even Fibonacci set

nodes.summary: Write $F_n$ for the $n$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. A natural number $d$ belongs to the positive Fibonacci set if and only if $d = F_n$ for some natural number $n \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Membership in the positive Fibonacci set

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of natural numbers and let $r, s$ be natural numbers with $1 \le r \le s$. If $D$ is $s$-accessible, then $D$ is $r$-accessible.
nodes.title: Accessibility with more colors implies accessibility with fewer

nodes.summary: Write $f_n$ for the $n$-th Fibonacci number ($f_0 = 0$, $f_1 = 1$). Let $F = \{1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots\}$ be the set of positive Fibonacci numbers and $G = \{f_{3n}/2 : n \ge 1\} = \{1, 4, 17, 72, \dots\}$ the set of halves of the even Fibonacci numbers. If $G$ is not $2$-accessible, then $F$ is not $4$-accessible.
nodes.title: Halved even Fibonacci numbers and $4$-accessibility of the Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$. Suppose there are a real number $\delta > 0$ and a natural number $N \ge 1$ such that $d_{n+1} \ge (3 + \delta) d_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n + 1 \ge N$. Then $D$ is not $2$-accessible.
nodes.title: Fast eventual growth rules out 2-accessibility

nodes.summary: Let $d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers with $d_0 > 0$ and $d_{n+1} \ge 3 d_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $D = \{d_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$. Then $D$ is not $2$-large.
nodes.title: Sets growing by a factor of three are not 2-large

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients, positive leading coefficient and $p(0) = 0$. Then the set of positive integers $d$ such that $p(n) = d$ for some positive integer $n$ is large.
nodes.title: Positive values of a polynomial vanishing at zero form a large set

nodes.summary: The positive Fibonacci set is $\{F_n : n \ge 2\}$, where the Fibonacci numbers are $F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$ and $F_{n+2} = F_{n+1} + F_n$. Equivalently, it is the set $\{1, 2, 3, 5, 8, \dots\}$ of positive Fibonacci numbers, each counted once.
nodes.title: Positive Fibonacci set

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number. If a set $D \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is $r$-large and $F \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is finite, then $D \setminus F$ is $r$-large.
nodes.title: Finite removal preserves $r$-largeness

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of positive integers. Say that $D$ has *diffsequence recurrence* if for every compact metric space $X$, every minimal homeomorphism $T$ of $X$, every nonempty open set $U \subseteq X$ and every $k \ge 1$ there are integers $s_1, \dots, s_k$ forming a $D$-diffsequence such that $U \cap T^{-s_1}U \cap \dots \cap T^{-s_k}U$ is nonempty, where $T^{-s}U$ is the preimage of $U$ under the integer power…
nodes.title: Topological recurrence, accessibility and chromatic intersectivity

nodes.summary: The morphism $\mu$ on binary words sends the letter $0$ to the word $10$ and the letter $1$ to the word $01$.
nodes.title: The Thue–Morse morphism $\mu$

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $D_1, D_2 \subseteq \mathbb{N}$. If $D_1 \cup D_2$ is a set of $k$-topological recurrence, then $D_1$ or $D_2$ is a set of $k$-topological recurrence.
nodes.title: One part of a union inherits $k$-topological recurrence

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of positive integers. If for every $k \ge 1$ there are positive integers $x_1, \dots, x_k$, all in $D$, that form a $D$-diffsequence, then $D$ is $2$-accessible.
nodes.title: Sets containing their own long diffsequences are 2-accessible

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a set of positive integers, let $\alpha$ be a real number and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be such that $\lVert \alpha d \rVert \ge \varepsilon$ for every $d \in D$, where $\lVert t \rVert$ denotes the distance from $t$ to the nearest integer. Then there is a $2$-coloring of the positive integers with no monochromatic $D$-arithmetic progression of length $\lceil 1/(2\varepsilon) \rceil + 1$.
nodes.title: Two-colorings avoiding long $D$-progressions

nodes.summary: Every $2$-large set $D$ of positive integers contains a multiple of each positive integer $m$.
nodes.title: 2-large sets contain multiples of every positive integer

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ with $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, Wesley's constant satisfies $c_{n,0} = 2/5$.
nodes.title: Wesley's constant $c_{n,0}$ for $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and an integer $\varepsilon$, the real number $c_{n,\varepsilon}$ is defined by the residue of $n$ modulo $4$: if $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$, then $c_{n,\varepsilon} = (4 + (2\sqrt5 - 5)\varepsilon)/10$; if $n \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then $c_{n,\varepsilon} = (11 - 4\sqrt5)/5$ when $\varepsilon = -4$ and $c_{n,\varepsilon} = (4 + (4\sqrt5 - 5)\varepsilon)/20$ otherwise; if $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, then…
nodes.title: Wesley's constants $c_{n,\varepsilon}$

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be the morphism of binary words with $0 \mapsto 10$ and $1 \mapsto 01$, and let $f_0 = 0$, $f_1 = 01$, $f_2 = 010$, $\dots$ be the finite Fibonacci words. The word $S$ is the infinite binary word, indexed from $0$, whose letter at index $n$ is the letter at index $n$ of $\mu(f_{n+2})$.
nodes.title: Wesley's word $S$

nodes.summary: Let $\nu$ be the morphism of binary words with $0 \mapsto 1$ and $1 \mapsto 00$, and let $f_0 = 0$, $f_1 = 01$, $f_2 = 010$, $\dots$ be the finite Fibonacci words. The word $T$ is the infinite binary word, indexed from $0$, whose letter at index $n$ is the letter at index $n$ of $\nu(f_{n+2})$.
nodes.title: Wesley's word $T$

nodes.summary: Indexing letters from $0$, the letters of $S$ at indices $0, 1, \dots, 9$ are $1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1$ and the letters of $T$ at indices $0, 1, \dots, 9$ are $1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0$; that is, $S$ begins with $1001101001$ and $T$ begins with $1001100100$.
nodes.title: The first ten letters of Wesley's words $S$ and $T$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
